subject: reviewer independence from the artifact under review
scenario: A reviewer that can fix what it finds is faster and produces a cleaner diff. It also stops being a reviewer: nobody independent has looked at the code that now exists, and the finding it would have raised is now a change it made silently. The opposite error is cheaper to make and was made here: a reviewer with no write access at all cannot record the verdict every acceptance predicate reads, so a real architecture review produced findings and had nowhere to put them. Failure looks like: A reviewer profile gains write access to a path outside docs/reviews/**. A reviewer's write scope is emptied, which reads like the stronger rule and silently removes the organization's ability to record a verdict.
expected_behaviors: Every role whose name contains 'review' has an allow-mode write scope.
That scope is docs/reviews/** and nothing else, so a reviewer can record its verdict and cannot author what it reviews.
No reviewer has an empty write scope: a reviewer that cannot write cannot record the verdict the agent_verdict predicates read.
No peer reviewer in any department cycle can write the artifact that cycle reviews.
failure_conditions: A reviewer profile gains Write or Edit.
A reviewer role is moved onto an implementer profile.
A cycle's peer reviewer becomes a worker in the same cycle.
A single-worker cycle declares mutual peer review, which is self-review with a second name.

checks.description: The role that evaluates agents cannot edit the agents it evaluates.

checks.pattern: The author never reviews its own change

notes: Independence here is structural rather than behavioural: it does not depend on a reviewer choosing to keep its hands off, because the tool profile removes the option. CYCLE-PROD is the one place the guarantee rests on write scope instead of the tool list, and validate_plugin.py already warns about it.
